name: laptop_dmic
_notes: Stand-in array: the ThinkPad T14s' 2-channel DMIC pair on the lid (owner B's dev profile).
Same shape as config/array.json so ingest/DOA/fusion are geometry-agnostic; swapping in the
hat is `--profile hat` and nothing else. This is NOT the wearable and must never be claimed as it.
Channels are the device channel order from pw-record (audio.position FL,FR): 0 = left, 1 = right.
x is the hat frame axis (0deg bearing = +y = nose); with the lid as the array, +x = wearer right.
spacing_m starts null: the real value is measured, never assumed. The measured value is
filled in automatically by `server/main.py --fit-spacing write`, which borrows the camera
bearing while someone talks (server/calib_fit.py) and writes back into this file.
Until then DOA still measures the real sign, and accuracy_deg is deliberately huge.
highpass_hz/lowpass_hz are set to the DOA band itself: channel 1 arrives with a 16%-of-FS DC
offset (+5390 LSB) and ~12 dB more LF energy than channel 0, so an RMS detector working on the
channel mean sees the rumble rather than the sound (a clap rose 5.6 dB unfiltered vs 26 dB
filtered, and 0 vs all onsets detected). The band is not a claim about the mics: a speaker-played
650 Hz tone arrives at 41 dB in-band SNR and live speech classifies as Speech at 44.6 dB.
analysis_channels names the capsule the classifier and transcriber hear. Measured on this
laptop: both capsules are equally clean in-band (-57 dB in 300-3000 Hz), but channel 1 carries
a +11645 LSB DC offset (36% of full scale) and a sub-100 Hz rumble 31 dB louder than channel 0
(-26.7 vs -47.7 dB). Averaging the pair feeds that rumble to YAMNet and to every level meter,
which is what makes the raw signal look 'weird'. Channel 0 is the clean one.
The real limitation of this pair is the missing baseline: three independent measurements put the
effective inter-channel spacing below ~5 mm, so azimuth is not recoverable here and the DOA gate
correctly refuses. The hat's 240 mm baseline is a real baseline. See docs/backend-evidence.md 4.
device: the PipeWire node name of the DMIC array; null = whatever the default source is.
